assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data evidence on intergenerational mobility has reshaped the empirical study of opportunity and place.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are central identifiable contributors to the listed research programme.
assessment.maturity: The measurement framework and associated findings have been extensively used across economics and policy research.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between the measurement programme and its many subsequent applications remains difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work supplied influential evidence and a coherent account of how trade, technology, and task change affect local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson provide a clear core attribution for the trade-shock and labour-demand contribution.
assessment.maturity: Its empirical designs, concepts, and conclusions have generated a large, sustained research literature.
uncertainties: Causal mechanisms and the relative importance of trade versus technological change continue to be actively debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence and audit approaches made labour-market discrimination directly measurable with unusually transparent empirical designs.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are prominent and readily attributable architects of the flagship correspondence-study contribution.
assessment.maturity: The approach is established, widely replicated, and consequential for empirical labour economics.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates capture important dimensions of discrimination but do not by themselves identify every mechanism or all labour-market effects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme connected rigorous insurance theory with credible empirical measurement of selection and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie form a plausible, complementary set of central contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become a durable reference point for insurance, health, and public-economics research.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several related theoretical and empirical strands, complicating a single sharply bounded prize citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on monopsony transformed the analysis of wage setting and employer power from a peripheral possibility into a central empirical question.
assessment.attribution: Manning is especially central to the modern framework, with Ashenfelter and Naidu important contributors to its empirical development.
assessment.maturity: The topic has matured into a major labour-economics literature with broad relevance for wage policy.
uncertainties: The magnitude and institutional sources of labour-market power vary substantially across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work established early-life conditions and skill formation as central economic determinants of later outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha represent complementary empirical and conceptual pillars of the listed contribution.
assessment.maturity: The insights have persisted across health, education, labour, and public economics.
uncertainties: The candidate description combines distinct literatures whose precise joint attribution is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification provided a foundational alternative to over-precise inference when economic data and assumptions cannot point-identify parameters.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the principal intellectual anchor, while Tamer and Molinari are major contributors to the listed econometric development.
assessment.maturity: The methods are well established and influential across applied econometrics.
uncertainties: Its broad methodological character makes the most appropriate three-person attribution less clear than for a single empirical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural methods for demand, competition, and dynamic industry behaviour materially expanded what industrial organization could measure and evaluate.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Pakes, and Bresnahan are central figures in the development of the programme.
assessment.maturity: These methods have become standard components of modern empirical industrial organization.
uncertainties: The programme has many major contributors, so a three-person laureate set necessarily leaves consequential work outside the citation.
